proof:
Role: this replaces step 3 of the parent-supplied proof, which uses separability of C([−s, s]) via ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace; that instance is not in the import closure of GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean.
0. If d ≤ c then (c, d) = ∅. Take F_n := 0, which is C¹ with empty tsupport; the conclusion is vacuous. From now on assume c < d and write J := (c, d).
1. (Plateau functions.) Let σ := Real.smoothTransition: C^∞, 0 ≤ σ ≤ 1, σ = 0 on (−∞, 0] and σ = 1 on [1, ∞). For p < q and k ∈ ℕ put χ_{p,q,k}(α) := σ(k(α − p))·σ(k(q − α)). Then:
   - χ_{p,q,k} is C^∞, hence C¹, and 0 ≤ χ_{p,q,k} ≤ 1.
   - χ_{p,q,k}(α) = 0 unless p < α < q (if α ≤ p the first argument is ≤ 0; if α ≥ q the second is), so tsupport χ_{p,q,k} ⊆ [p, q].
   - χ_{p,q,k}(α) → 1_{(p,q)}(α) as k → ∞, for every α. If p < α < q, both arguments are ≥ 1 once k ≥ 1/(α − p) and k ≥ 1/(q − α), so the value is eventually 1. Otherwise the value is 0 for every k.
2. (Enumeration.) ℚ × ℚ × ℕ is countable and nonempty, so there is a surjection e : ℕ → ℚ × ℚ × ℕ (exists_surjective_nat). Define F_n := χ_{p,q,k} if e(n) = (p, q, k) with c < p < q < d, and F_n := 0 otherwise. Every F_n is C¹, and tsupport F_n ⊆ [p, q] ⊆ J or tsupport F_n = ∅.
3. (Rational intervals.) Let w be integrable on J with ∫ F_n w = 0 for all n, and let w̄ := 1_J·w; it is integrable on ℝ (IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator). Fix rationals c < p < q < d. For each k choose n with e(n) = (p, q, k). Then ∫ χ_{p,q,k}·w̄ = ∫ F_n·w = 0; the two integrands coincide because χ_{p,q,k} vanishes off J. The functions χ_{p,q,k}·w̄ are dominated by |w̄| and converge pointwise to 1_{(p,q)}·w̄ (step 1). By dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence), ∫_{(p,q)} w̄ = lim_k ∫ χ_{p,q,k}·w̄ = 0.
4. (Primitive.) Let W(x) := ∫_c^x w̄ (interval integral). W is continuous on ℝ (intervalIntegral.continuous_primitive, since w̄ is integrable) and W(c) = 0. For rationals c < p < q < d:
   W(q) − W(p) = ∫_p^q w̄ = ∫_{(p,q]} w̄ = ∫_{(p,q)} w̄ = 0
   (intervalIntegral.integral_interval_sub_left, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, step 3).
   Fix a rational q₀ ∈ J (exists_rat_btwn). Then W = W(q₀) on ℚ ∩ J. The closure of ℚ ∩ J contains [c, d], because between any two reals there is a rational. By continuity W = W(q₀) on [c, d] (Set.EqOn.of_subset_closure). Evaluating at c gives W ≡ 0 on [c, d].
5. (Lebesgue differentiation.) Lebesgue measure on ℝ is uniformly locally doubling (the instance IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure (volume : Measure ℝ) is available). Apply Mathlib IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average to the locally integrable w̄, with K := 1, the constant centre x and radius ρ, along the filter 𝓝[>] 0; note x ∈ closedBall x (1·ρ) for ρ > 0. It gives: for a.e. x ∈ ℝ, the averages ⨍_{closedBall x ρ} w̄ converge to w̄(x) as ρ → 0⁺. Let x ∈ J be such a point. For 0 < ρ < min(x − c, d − x):
   - closedBall x ρ = [x − ρ, x + ρ] ⊆ [c, d] (Real.closedBall_eq_Icc);
   - ∫_{[x−ρ, x+ρ]} w̄ = W(x + ρ) − W(x − ρ) = 0 (integral_Icc_eq_integral_Ioc and step 4);
   - so the average vanishes (setAverage_eq).
   Hence w(x) = w̄(x) = lim 0 = 0. Therefore w = 0 almost everywhere on J. ∎
(An equivalent finish to step 5: since w̄ = 0 off J, W ≡ 0 on all of ℝ. So the finite measures with densities w̄⁺ and w̄⁻ agree on every interval (a', b'] and on ℝ. Measure.ext_of_Ioc_finite then gives equality of these measures, whence w̄ = 0 a.e.)
key_steps: Smooth plateaus χ_{p,q,k}(α) = σ(k(α−p))σ(k(q−α)) are C¹, supported in [p,q], bounded by 1, and converge pointwise to 1_{(p,q)}.
Enumerate the rational triples (p,q,k) with c<p<q<d by a surjection ℕ → ℚ×ℚ×ℕ to define F_n.
Dominated convergence gives ∫_{(p,q)} w = 0 for all rational c<p<q<d.
The continuous primitive W of 1_J·w is constant on ℚ∩J, hence W ≡ 0 on [c,d].
Lebesgue differentiation (IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average) gives w = 0 a.e. on (c,d).
